title: Inert-operad algebras are color diagrams without presentability
statement:
Use the universe, quasicategory and monoidal infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], using only its definitions, and inert base maps of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $p:\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad whose zero-fiber is a Kan complex. Let $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{int}}$ have all objects of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and precisely its inert arrows. Put
$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}=\mathcal M\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{int}},$$
viewed over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ via the inclusion, and let $\tau:\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathcal M$ be the projection. Then $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$ is a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad, $\tau$ preserves inert arrows, and its zero-fiber map is the identity of $\mathcal M_{[0]}$. For every monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V$, with no cocompleteness or presentability assumption, evaluation on the fiber over $[1]$ induces an equivalence
$$E_{\mathcal V}:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathcal V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M_{[1]},\mathcal V).$$
This equivalence is natural under inert-preserving precomposition in $\mathcal M$ and lax monoidal postcomposition in $\mathcal V$, including coherent transformations and their higher homotopies. In particular, for a lax monoidal $F:\mathcal V\to\mathcal W$, if $F_*^{\mathrm{triv}}$ is postcomposition on inert-operad algebras and $G=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M_{[1]},F)$, then $E_{\mathcal W}F_*^{\mathrm{triv}}\simeq GE_{\mathcal V}$, and $E_{\mathcal V}\tau^*$ is the functor evaluating an $\mathcal M$-algebra on its colors.

source.place: Gepner-Haugseng, Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5; naturality is that of restriction and postcomposition. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic result.

proof.text: The inert arrows in the statement are exactly the opposites of consecutive-subinterval inclusions, as in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. The generalized operad definition in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] uses the full incidence diagram of projections to both $[0]$ and $[1]$, precisely the definition in [lem-coef-inert-operad-color-reconstruction]. Thus the latter applies to the given small $\mathcal M$, its Kan zero-fiber, and the arbitrary monoidal $\mathcal V$. We use no presentability assertion of the definition-bearing node.

source.place: Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1 and Proposition 3.4.5; naturality of the actual restriction functor.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-inert-operad-color-reconstruction]. Its pullback $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$ is the pullback displayed here, since its base subcategory has all objects and precisely the inert arrows. Its conclusions give smallness, the generalized operad axioms, preservation of inert edges by $\tau$, and $\tau_{[0]}=\mathrm{id}$. They also give the equivalence $E_{\mathcal V}$ by actual restriction to the $[1]$-fiber, including transformations and all higher simplices, without colimit or presentability assumptions. The $[1]$-fiber of the pullback is $\mathcal M_{[1]}$, since pullback along the inert subcategory does not change any fiber.

source.place: Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1 and Proposition 3.4.5; naturality of the actual restriction functor.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal N$ be another small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad with Kan zero-fiber, let $u:\mathcal N\to\mathcal M$ be a functor over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving inert edges, and let $u_{\mathrm{triv}}:\mathcal N_{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$ be its restriction (it lies over the base). The inert edges of $\mathcal N_{\mathrm{triv}}$ are exactly the inert edges of $\mathcal N$: since the base mapping spaces are discrete and inert maps are closed under composition, the mapping spaces of $\mathcal N_{\mathrm{triv}}$ over an inert $\gamma$ are those of $\mathcal N$, so an $\mathcal N$-cocartesian edge over an inert map stays cocartesian, and an $\mathcal N_{\mathrm{triv}}$-cocartesian edge is equivalent in the common target fiber to the $\mathcal N$-cocartesian lift with the same source. The same holds for $\mathcal M$. Hence $u_{\mathrm{triv}}$ preserves inert edges and $A\circ u_{\mathrm{triv}}$ is an $\mathcal N_{\mathrm{triv}}$-algebra for every $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$-algebra $A$. For an algebra diagram $A$, restriction gives $E_{\mathcal V}(A\circ u_{\mathrm{triv}})=(E_{\mathcal V}A)\circ u_{[1]}$. For a lax monoidal $F$ as defined in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], composition with $F$ preserves the inert-preserving condition; writing $F_{[1]}$ for its underlying functor, restriction gives $E_{\mathcal W}(F\circ A)=F_{[1]}\circ E_{\mathcal V}(A)$. These identities hold for diagrams $A:K\times\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over the base for every simplicial parameter $K$, and for parameterized pre- and postcomposition as well: both sides restrict the same composite to $K\times\mathcal M_{[1]}$. Restriction to faces and degeneracies of $K$ commutes with these identities. They therefore give naturality on coherent transformations and all higher homotopies, and in particular $E_{\mathcal W}F_*^{\mathrm{triv}}\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M_{[1]},F_{[1]})E_{\mathcal V}$.

source.place: Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1 and Proposition 3.4.5; naturality of the actual restriction functor.

proof.text: For an $\mathcal M$-algebra $B$, the composite $E_{\mathcal V}\tau^*$ restricts $B$ first along $\tau$ and then to the $[1]$-fiber. Their composite inclusion is exactly $\mathcal M_{[1]}\hookrightarrow\mathcal M$. Hence it sends $B$ to its color diagram, with the same identity on parameterized transformations. This proves the final assertion.
